newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds continue slide, seen falling more.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds continue slide, seen falling more.

text.p: Argentine bonds were much lower again late Friday morning as the market continued to be hammered by the fallout of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's statements earlier in the week.
"The market is still very nervous and this could go on a day or two more," said the head bond trader at an Argentine bank.
He reported, however, that so far in the session there had been no heavy selling by funds as seen in the two previous days.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 5/8 to 89-7/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.32 to 125.50.
Traders maintained their medium-term positive outlook on the market, arguing that the lower prices will attract buyers soon.
"We are getting closer to the market's floor but it is still nervous today, so I would wait until next week (to buy)," said another trader.
